_comment: Acceptance scenes for the voxel diorama. Data, not code, so adding a scene
is one entry and never a change to the runner.
Rewritten 2026-09-01. The first version was written BACKWARDS: the [stats]
line came first and checks were written against whatever it exposed, so a
scene could pass on 'carved == 0' while drawing its roof twice. These
criteria encode OBJECT INTEGRITY instead - the 2D art reinterpreted as
coherent 3D objects: one drawing is one object, at one height, with one
classification, drawn once. Every rectangle below was verified against the
decomp's own map grids (data/layouts/*/map.bin, stitched the way the game
stitches Oldale above and Littleroot below Route 101) so it contains WHOLE
objects, and every expected count was derived from those grids, not from
the mesher. They are written to FAIL against the mesher as of this date.
Counts assume the ruby_usa.state1 snapshot (player on Route 101, Oldale and
Littleroot stitched into the 35x34 backup window). A different save
position stitches different neighbours and changes the whole-map numbers.
isolate: 'x,y,w,h' lifts that rectangle of the map onto empty ground.
omit it to render the whole assembled map.
checks:  assertions against the [stats] line the mesher prints, and the
[object] lines that follow it. Each is {field, op, value}.
Integer fields: vertices objects masses carved boxed tufts dupart.
ops: eq min max.
'heights' takes op 'only' (the set of column extents present must
be exactly this list) or 'max'.
'objects' with op 'list' matches the [object] lines as a MULTISET
of {w,h,extent,class}: w x h is the footprint's bounding box in
cells, extent the art rows, class prop or structure. A count alone
is not a criterion - nine tree halves can total nine objects.
watch:   what a human should look for. NOT machine-checked - it is printed
beside the render in the report so the eye knows where to go.

scenes.name: route101
scenes.title: The whole assembled map
watch: Forests read as individual round trees, not one fused mass and not two half-blobs per tree
Classification tile: yellow forests, red buildings, grey ground, no slab of red where a forest is
The Oldale house's east wall is present behind the trees at (25,1)-(26,4)
No roof art lying on the grass behind either building

scenes.name: house
scenes.title: Oldale house - four rows, door on the bottom row (647)
watch: ONE building at ONE height with ONE roof - no towers, no notch over the door
Door and ground-floor windows at ground level, first-floor windows above them, roof above that
No eroded rounded pillar at either corner
Roof rises to a ridge and falls back - not a ramp; no gap under the north eave
No roof art lying on the grass behind the building

scenes.name: pokecenter
scenes.title: Pokemon Centre - four rows, door on the bottom row (97)
watch: One building, one roof: the Pokeball logo appears ONCE, on the roof, not again up the facade
Facade reads: sliding door and P.C sign at ground level, walls showing their own art not grass
No notch at the rounded ground-floor corners (96/99)
No roof art lying on the grass behind the building

scenes.name: tree
scenes.title: One tree - 468/469 canopy over 476/477 base
watch: ONE tree, not two half-blobs of different heights
The two halves join across the seam into one round crown
Plain grass underneath - no tree-shaped patch on the floor
The crown stays inside the tree's own 2x2 plot

scenes.name: trees-stacked
scenes.title: Two stacked trees whose canopy and base variants differ (468 471 / 476 477 / 468 469 / 484 487)
watch: Two trees of the same height, one behind the other - not one four-cell tower
Each canopy sits on its own base; the front tree does not wear the back tree's trunk

scenes.name: forest
scenes.title: A block of forest - one tree, then five in a row
watch: Six distinct trees with gaps, not a hedge
No tree noticeably taller than its neighbours
Tall grass tufts in front of the row stay ankle-high

scenes.name: ledge
scenes.title: A ledge (110 135 135 135 214 / 213 135 135 135 142) - must NOT stand
watch: The ledge lies flat - a lip at most, nothing a metre tall across the route
The rounded end cap (110) is a small lump, not a post

scenes.name: littleroot-clipped
scenes.title: A Littleroot house cut off by the map border - the only door-less structure on the window
watch: Solid - no black notches you can see through
Ridged roof survives the fallback path; no gable-end holes on the flanks
Roof planks appear once, on the roof, not again down the wall
